paper.title_en: Vortex solitons in spin-orbit-coupled atomic-molecular condensates
paper.abstract_en: In our previous study of a three-dimensional (3D) atomic-molecular Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) with quadratic nonlinearity and spin-orbit coupling (SOC), stable solitons are realized as semi-vortex (SV) or mixed-mode (MM) states, with SOC applied solely to the atomic component. In the SV state, the molecular part forms a pure vortex, while the atomic part remains a hybrid of fundamental and vortex modes. This prevents the overall self-bound state from achieving a fully pure vortex configuration, with the total vortex component always less than $100\%$. Here, we extend the study to two dimensions (2D) and uncover a qualitatively different behavior: purely quadratic 2D systems support not only ground-state (GS) SV solitons, but also higher-order excited-state (ES) solitons that are genuine full vortices (a feature absent in the 3D counterpart). For both GS and ES solitons, stable vortex states exist only when the SOC strength $λ$ exceeds a minimum threshold $λ_{\min}$, which increases monotonically with $S_1$. Conversely, the critical detuning $α_c$ decreases monotonically with $S_1$, indicating that higher-order vortices are more susceptible to destabilization. For $λ< λ_{\min}$, the system forms MM states instead of vortex solitons. Our results demonstrate that dimensional reduction to 2D enables the emergence of pure-vortex excited states, establishing a new pathway for stabilizing high-charge topological excitations in ultracold molecular gases.
